leads.summary: Included Kitty face overrides remain on the old family
leads.consequence: With kitty.conf containing `include extra.conf` and extra.conf containing `bold_font Old Font`, one `omarchy font set 'Test Font'` appends `font_family Test Font` to kitty.conf but does not touch or override the included bold_font. Kitty reads the included directive, so bold continues to request Old Font after the first and every later run. This matters to users who separate font choices into included config files; the new direct-line test does not exercise them.
leads.triage: pre-existing and unchanged from base (Opus followup-1); already disclosed in prior test scope; restated in test scope, not a finding

leads.summary: A valid continued face directive becomes a different, concatenated family
leads.consequence: Kitty accepts `bold_font ` followed by a physical line `\Old Font` as `bold_font Old Font`. The sed loop replaces only the first physical line with `bold_font Test Font`, leaving the continuation untouched; Kitty then joins it into `bold_font Test FontOld Font`. The command exits 0 and repeats the malformed selection on every run, rather than setting the chosen family. The same boundary applies to each of the three face keys.
leads.triage: behavioural: neutral follow-up to Opus, confirmed in followup-1 (emulated kitty 0.49.1 parser); published as Optional rare edge case (N3)

leads.summary: Coordinate the face-loop conflict with the competing open Kitty fix
leads.location: bin/omarchy-font-set:41-49; open PR #9168 bin/omarchy-font-set diff at @@ -38,6 +38,7 @@
leads.consequence: Open #9168 fixes the same issue but intentionally changes every explicit Kitty face to `auto`, whereas this PR writes the selected bare family and preserves an existing `auto`. The heads diverge, and a merge against #9168's own base produces conflict markers over precisely this loop. Whichever revision merges second requires an explicit choice of intended face behavior; taking either conflict side discards the other. Other open changes to this command, notably #12457 (escaping), #10811 (font validation/escaping) and #8179 (XDG path), also have textual conflicts; avoid dropping the face loop or the name escaping during resolution.
leads.triage: #9168 conflict corroborated by Opus final (related/mt.9168) and verified with gh (Fixes #9167, auto approach); published as related-PR note with #13235. #12457/#8179 conflicts dropped as ordinary merge coordination

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12171#issuecomment-5836641025), checked at head `98b24eb` after the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12171#issuecomment-5846470891). Both earlier findings are addressed. No material regressions from the new commit were found in the tested scope; one rare edge case is noted below.

| Earlier finding | At `98b24eb` |
|---|---|
| Faces stay stale when `kitty.conf` has no active `font_family` | **Resolved** |
| Deliberate per-face choices are overwritten | **Addressed:** the PR description now documents this as the intended behavior |
| Earlier **Verified** list | Still holds, now on both branches of the `if` |

### Resolved: faces now sync on the first font set

**Verified:** the escaped name is now computed before the `if`, and the face loop runs after both branches. One `omarchy font set "Test Font"` on the shipped template with hand-added faces now gives:

```text
kitty.conf before                 after, prior head 31d682d        after, head 98b24eb
--------------------------------  -------------------------------  -------------------------------
# font_family JetBrainsMono ...   # font_family JetBrainsMono ...  # font_family JetBrainsMono ...
bold_font Old Font                bold_font Old Font   (stale)     bold_font Test Font
italic_font auto                  italic_font auto                 italic_font auto
                                  font_family Test Font            font_family Test Font
```

The same holds for a file with only face lines, an empty file, a missing file with kitty present, a symlinked `kitty.conf`, sed metacharacters in the name (`A&B/C\D Mono`) and tab or indentation variants. Repeated runs keep one active `font_family`, and a second identical run changes nothing. The new test case fails against the `31d682d` script (`not ok - font command updates a stale face before font_family exists`) and passes on `98b24eb`. The earlier stale-faces test still fails against the base script. The Alacritty, Ghostty and foot output is byte-identical across base, `31d682d` and `98b24eb`.

### Addressed: scope of face replacement

The PR description now says every non-`auto` face, including a different family or a `kitten choose-fonts` spec, is replaced, matching the Alacritty branch. Behavior is unchanged from the earlier review and now also applies on the append branch. Whether to keep this scope is a maintainer decision.

**Optional, rare edge case:** a face value that kitty reads across a `\` continuation line (for example `bold_font family="Old Font"` followed by `\ style=Heavy`) keeps its second line. Only the first line is rewritten, so kitty joins them into `Test Font style=Heavy`, a family name that does not exist. This needs a hand-split face line. Since `98b24eb` it also happens when `font_family` is not active; before, such a line stayed as the old, valid spec. The existing `font_family` rewrite behaves the same at base. Removing continuation lines that directly follow a rewritten key line would cover both. The kitty values here come from its 0.49.1 config parser source, applied to the script's output; kitty itself was not run.

**Optional documentation note:** the PR description says kitty is "the only managed terminal with separate config lines per face". Ghostty (`font-family-bold`, `font-family-italic`, `font-family-bold-italic`) and foot (`font-bold`, `font-italic`, `font-bold-italic`) have per-face keys as well, and `omarchy font set` leaves them unchanged. The shipped Ghostty and foot templates do not set them, so this is pre-existing and outside the diff. Rewording that sentence, or noting those keys as out of scope, would avoid the inaccuracy.

**Related open PRs:** [#9168](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/9168) and [#13235](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13235) also target #9167. #9168 resets the faces to `auto` instead and conflicts textually with this PR in `bin/omarchy-font-set`. #13235 merges without conflicts, but the combined script would have two face loops.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Follow-up source review of head `98b24eba512ab1a0d4d4ffd0760f8205edfd1cf6` against the earlier reviewed head `31d682d` and base `45748a2`, with kitty 0.49.1, Ghostty 1.3.1 and foot source read for the dependency claims. Sandboxed runs with a synthetic home and stubbed `fc-list`/`pkill`: the PR's `kitty-config-test.sh` on each revision and with the older scripts swapped in, the same test on a local merge with the current `quattro` base branch, `bin-style-test.sh`, and about 30 edge-case configs, including continuation lines and `include`d files, against all three scripts. kitty was not installed in the sandbox, so its native config check was skipped and rendering was not tested. `./test/cli` and the full `./test/shell` suite were not run. Faces set in `include`d files are still not followed by the script, as in the earlier review.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review with a targeted follow-up question and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
